1/1 steps, after one in-session correction. INITIAL FINDING (testability refutation, fixed in place with amend-step per this tier's rule that a testability-only finding does not spend a re-plan round): the declared check_email_templates.py acceptance test can never pass, on any artefact this step could legitimately produce. Verified directly -- ran `python3 skills/admin/email-templates-and-alerts/scripts/check_email_templates.py --manifest-dir <dir containing only a .flow-meta.xml file>` and got exit 1, ERROR 'no email template artefact found', because that checker only scans `.email`/`.email-meta.xml` files and this step deliberately produces none (the email content is inline inside the Flow's own emailSimple action, per Q11/D1 -- the whole point of choosing Send Email over an Email Alert). A test that fails on every possible correct output is not a test with an inverted pass condition, it is not applicable to this step at all. Removed via `amend-step --file <acceptance_tests, inputs>` (legal at status `planned`, which allows exactly those two fields), with the reason and the checker's own error output recorded in the amendment and in inputs.email_templates_checker_note. Re-verified the remaining 3 tests directly and for real, not from memory: (1) check_record_triggered_flow_patterns.py --manifest-dir <the actual built artefact directory> -> 'No issues found.', exit 0; a negative fixture with every faultConnector stripped -> 7 ERROR lines (one per DML/action/lookup element) and exit 1, proving the test can fail; (2) `python3 scripts/build_plan.py check-outputs <plan> M1-S01` -> `{"ok": true, "missing": [], "empty": [], "malformed": []}`, confirming the xml test's premise (every declared file exists, is non-empty, and the two XML files parse); (3) manifest: package.xml's sole <types><name>Flow</name><members>Case_Escalation_Notify_Account_Owner</members> matches the built flow file's base name exactly, satisfying the manifest test by inspection. Metadata coverage: automation is a metadata type in scope, and this step (owned by metadata-builder, not apex-builder) both an xml and a manifest test, and package.xml is declared in outputs[] -- the always-on manifest row is satisfied. Scope agrees with command: the remaining checker test declares scope: step and its command reads --manifest-dir artefacts/M1-S01, matching. Milestone M1 carries its own manual acceptance test. Human gate: this step changes no access and deletes nothing, so human_gate: false is correct and not refuted. Manual-test-observable-only-in-a-deployed-org WARN (not a refutation at scale: feature, per this tier's own rule): M1's manual test partially depends on an actual email arriving in an inbox, which only a deployed org produces; flagged as a WARN the human weighs at the plan gate, consistent with how this tier treats that row. 1 warning.
